title: The Geometric Distribution: Model Assumptions and Exact Term Probabilities

questions.title: Exact Term in a Standard Geometric Model

parts.text: A fair six-sided die is rolled repeatedly until a 5 is obtained. Let $X$ be the number of rolls required. Find $P(X = 4)$, giving your answer as an exact fraction and as a decimal correct to 4 significant figures.

questions.title: Geometric Probability with Decimal Success Parameter

parts.text: Independent trials are performed where the probability of success on each trial is $p = 0.35$. Let $X$ be the number of trials up to and including the first success. Find $P(X = 3)$, giving your answer as an exact decimal.

questions.title: First Prime Number on a Numbered Spinner

parts.text: A fair spinner has 5 equal sections numbered $1, 2, 3, 4, 5$. The spinner is spun repeatedly until a prime number is obtained. Let $X$ be the number of spins required. Find $P(X = 2)$.

A bag contains 6 red counters and 4 white counters. Counters are removed one at a time at random, without replacement, until the first red counter is obtained. Let $X$ be the number of counters removed. Find $P(X = 3)$, and state why $X$ does not follow a geometric distribution.
The random variable $X$ has a geometric distribution with parameter $p = 0.25$. Find the probability that the first success occurs on either the 2nd trial or the 3rd trial.

questions.title: Recovering Parameter p from First-Trial Probability

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has a geometric distribution such that $P(X = 1) = 0.40$. Find the value of $p$, and calculate $P(X = 3)$.

questions.title: Repeated Coin Tosses Until a Pair of Heads

parts.text: Two fair coins are tossed together repeatedly until a pair of heads is obtained. Let $X$ be the number of throws required. Find $P(X = 4)$, giving your answer as an exact fraction.
Find the probability that the first pair of heads occurs on either throw 2 or throw 3, giving your answer as an exact fraction in simplest form.

questions.title: Pair of Dice Sum Threshold and Early Throw Probabilities

parts.text: Two fair six-sided dice are thrown repeatedly. A throw is successful if the sum of the two scores is at least $10$. Let $X$ be the number of throws up to and including the first successful throw. Find the probability that the first successful throw occurs on throw 3, giving your answer as an exact fraction in simplest form.
Find the probability that the first successful throw occurs on throw 1, throw 2, or throw 3, giving your answer as an exact fraction in simplest form.

questions.title: Geometric Event Nested Inside a Binomial Trial Model

parts.text: In a target game, a contestant hits the bullseye with probability $0.30$ on any independent shot. Contestants take shots until they hit the bullseye. Let $A$ be the event that a contestant hits the bullseye for the first time on their 3rd shot. Find $P(A)$, giving your answer as an exact decimal.
Five independent contestants play this game. Find the probability that event $A$ occurs for exactly 2 of the 5 contestants, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

A box contains 4 red balls and 6 green balls. Balls are drawn one by one at random, without replacement, until the first green ball is obtained. Let $X$ be the number of draws required. Find the probability distribution of $X$, giving the probability for every possible value of $X$ as an exact fraction in simplest form.

Suppose instead that balls are drawn one by one with replacement until the first green ball is obtained. State the distribution of $X$, including its parameter, and calculate $P(X = 3)$ and $P(X \le 2)$.

questions.title: Ratio of Consecutive Geometric Terms and Even Positions

parts.text: A biased spinner is spun repeatedly until a specific outcome occurs. Let $X$ be the number of spins required, where $X \sim \text{Geo}(p)$. Given that $P(X = 2) = 1.2 \times P(X = 3)$, find the exact value of $p$.
Using $p = \frac{1}{6}$, find the probability that the first success occurs on an even-numbered spin in the first 4 spins (that is, $X = 2$ or $X = 4$), giving your answer as an exact fraction.

questions.title: Automated Quality Inspection: Odd-Numbered Trials to Shift Audits

parts.text: An automated inspection system inspects microchips passing along a production line. Defective microchips occur independently with a constant probability of $0.08$. Let $X$ be the number of microchips inspected up to and including the first defective microchip. Find $P(X = 5)$, giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.

Find the probability that the first defective microchip is detected on an odd-numbered microchip within the first 5 microchips inspected (that is, $X \in \{1, 3, 5\}$), giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.

Four independent production shifts are monitored. In each shift, let $E$ be the event that the first defective microchip is detected on an odd-numbered microchip within the first 5 microchips inspected. Find the probability that event $E$ occurs in at least 2 of the 4 shifts, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Two-Player Alternating Game: Truncated Geometric and Repeated Contests

parts.text: Players $A$ and $B$ take turns rolling a fair six-sided die, with Player $A$ rolling first. The game ends as soon as either player rolls a 6, and that player wins. Let $X$ be the total number of rolls made until the first 6 appears ($X \sim \text{Geo}\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)$). Player $A$ rolls on rolls 1, 3, and 5. Find the probability that Player $A$ wins the game within the first 5 rolls, giving your answer as an exact fraction in simplest form.
Player $B$ rolls on rolls 2 and 4. Find the probability that Player $B$ wins the game within the first 4 rolls, giving your answer as an exact fraction in simplest form.

Six independent games are played between Player $A$ and Player $B$. In each game, Player $A$ rolls first. Find the probability that Player $A$ wins within the first 5 rolls in at least 2 of the 6 games, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
